exercise.name: Smith Stiff Legged Deadlift

reference.title: Smith Stiff Legged Deadlift
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.bodyPart: Back of the thighs (hamstrings) and hips

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it while hinging down and back up, breathe out at the top.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.tempo: 2 s down, short pause, 1-1.5 s up
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: light enough to keep the back flat at the bottom, about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg once every rep reaches the same depth with a flat back.

cues.text: Stand tall in the Smith machine, feet hip width under the bar, bar in front of the thighs, overhand grip just outside the legs, arms straight. Turn the bar off the pegs; knees just unlocked and kept that way.
Push the hips straight back and lower the bar down the front of the legs with a flat back; the knees stay nearly straight.
Stop when the hamstrings are fully stretched, about mid-shin, before the back starts to round.
Drive the hips forward and stand up tall, the bar riding up the rails close to the legs.
Squeeze the glutes at the top without leaning back; re-brace for the next rep. After the last rep turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach lower
mistakes.fix: Only go as low as the hamstrings allow with a flat back; mid-shin is plenty.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the knees into a squat
mistakes.fix: Keep the soft knee angle fixed; the hips move back, not down.

mistakes.mistake: Bar drifting away from the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar close, lats tight, so it travels down the thighs and shins.
Finish with the hips under the shoulders and the glutes squeezed.

kinematics.norm: Deep hip hinge with a flat back; the knees stay almost straight so the hamstrings take more of the work than in a conventional deadlift (Lee 2018 for the straight-knee Romanian style)
Knees nearly straight, about 5-15 degrees, held through the rep (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈91° from vertical (≈-1° from level), back flat
kinematics.norm: Trunk near or a little below horizontal at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Smith rails 8.0° from vertical (top toward the front), bar 80.1 cm high at the top
kinematics.peak: 29.9 cm at the bottom (50.3 cm along the rails); hands' midpoint within 0.05 cm of the rail line at every key
kinematics.norm: Fixed by the guide rails: the bar can only travel along them (here a rail line fitted to the free-bar path, a few degrees from vertical at most); the feet sit so the bar stays close to the legs (common coaching)

kinematics.peak: 2.2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.4 s up, 1.3 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
Learn the hip hinge with a light load first; the back stays flat at every depth.
Low-back pain: shorten the range or bend the knees a little more.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Tight hamstrings: stop at the knees or just below.
Grip failing first: use straps for the top sets.
regressions: Hip hinge with a dowel along the back.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthened under load as the hips hinge with straight knees; they extend the hip on the way up (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthened under load as the hips hinge with straight knees; they extend the hip on the way up (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives the hips forward to stand tall.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drives the hips forward to stand tall.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat against the bar hanging in front (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat against the bar hanging in front (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the bar close to the legs.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the bar close to the legs.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the bar.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the bar.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the spine still while the hips move.
